sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Vikas Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- Afshan Shafaut,Amit Kumar Singh,G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned counsel for the High Court Legal Services Committee, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

2. The present second bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Special S.T. No.
280/2020, Case Crime No. 164 of 2019, under Section 376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act,
P.S. Lalauli, District Fatehpur with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
The first bail application of applicant was rejected by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 10.09.2020.

Rahul vs State Of U.P. on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14417494/
1 3.
It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant-accused is innocent and he has not committed any offence.

It was submitted that the alleged incident has been shown of 17.01.2019 but after that no report was lodged and later on an application under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C. was moved and case was registered on 25.06.2019 in pursuance of the order of court.
As per ossification test report, age of victim is 17 years and thus, by giving a margin of two years on upper side, she has to be treated as major girl.

It was further submitted that as per prosecution version,
applicant has come at the house of victim in the mid of day and committed rape upon her but there is nothing to show that victim has raised any alarm.
Victim has not sustained any injury.

4. It has further been submitted that first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 10.09.2020 and after that statement of victim has already been recorded before the trial court and thus, there is no possibility of tampering with the evidence.

It was further submitted that the applicant is in judicial custody since 17.02.2020 and thus, he has already undergone the detention of more than four years and that the trial of the case would take sufficient long time in its conclusion.
Lastly, it was submitted that in case applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail.

5. Learned A.G.A., learned counsel for the informant and learned counsel for the High Court Legal Services Committee have opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the first bail application of applicant has already been rejected by this Court on merits.
Victim is a minor girl and she has made allegation of rape against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the informant submits that the case of applicant regarding false implication is wholly improbable.

6. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the present second bail application is hereby allowed.

7. Let the applicant Rahul involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i. The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii.
The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant will not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
8. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 14.3.2024 Anand  Rahul vs State Of U.P. on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14417494/
